bugs.name: Watching a repository doesn't deliver a notification for a newly created issue
bugs.summary: The report says that a user watching a repository gets no notification when another user opens a new issue in it.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the watcher receives an unread notification for the new issue.
bugs.actual: After alex watched a new repository and eval opened an issue in it, alex's Unread notifications were reported to show only older entries, even after a refresh.
reproSteps: As one user, create a repository.
As a second user, watch the repository.
As the first user, open an issue in the repository.
As the second user, check Notifications > Unread.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced: watchers do get a notification for a new issue. Notifications are created by a background queue, so they arrive shortly after the issue is opened; in repeated runs, including the reported setup, the watcher's unread count went up with the new issue within a few seconds, and a manual repro confirmed it. The person who opens the issue is deliberately not notified of their own action ('dont notify user who cause notification' in models/activities/notification_list.go), so a report about the issue author not being notified is also intended.

bugs.name: A comment on a subscribed issue doesn't generate an unread notification
bugs.summary: The report says that after a user subscribes to an issue, another user's new comment on it (or an @mention of the subscriber in a comment) doesn't produce an unread notification for the subscriber.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the subscriber receives an unread notification for the new comment.
bugs.actual: After alex subscribed to an issue and eval commented on it, alex's Unread notifications were reported to show only older entries, even after a refresh; an @alex mention comment on the same issue was reported the same way.
reproSteps: As one user, create an issue.
As a second user, open the issue and click Subscribe.
As the first user, add a comment to the issue (optionally @mentioning the second user).
As the second user, check Notifications > Unread.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced: subscribers and mentioned users do get an unread notification for a new comment. Notifications are created by a background queue, so they arrive shortly after the comment is posted; in repeated runs the new notification appeared once the queue ran, a manual repro confirmed it works, and a user who wasn't subscribed correctly got nothing. The commenter is deliberately not notified of their own comment.

bugs.name: Pinning a notification marks another unread notification read
bugs.summary: The report says that pinning one notification also marks a different unread notification as read.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that pinning changes only the pinned notification, and other unread notifications stay unread.
bugs.actual: Pinning fresh notifications changed only the pinned one; every other unread notification stayed unread and the unread count dropped by exactly one, including after a reload.
reproSteps: Make sure the account has at least two unread notifications.
On the Notifications page, pin one of them.
Check whether the other notification is still unread.
bugs.reason: Not reproducible: the Pin action posts a single notification id, and the server updates only that notification. The only actions that mark other notifications read are Mark all as read and opening an issue, both intended. The report came from a run on an account shared with other agents, whose concurrent actions most likely changed the other notification.

bugs.name: Marking a pinned notification read clears another unread notification
bugs.summary: The report says that marking a pinned notification as read also marks a different unread notification as read.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that marking one notification as read leaves other unread notifications unread.
bugs.actual: Pinning a notification, marking all as read, marking another notification unread, and then marking the pinned one read left the other notification unread every time, including through the API.
reproSteps: Pin notification A and mark all notifications as read.
From the Read tab, mark notification B as unread.
Mark notification A as read.
Check whether notification B is still unread.
bugs.reason: Not reproducible: the Mark as read action posts a single notification id, and the server updates only that notification. The only actions that mark other notifications read are Mark all as read and opening an issue, both intended. The report came from a run on an account shared with other agents, whose concurrent actions most likely changed the other notification.

bugs.name: Pinned notification still opens the previous comment after an update
bugs.summary: The report says that after a new comment on a subscribed issue, the user's pinned notification moves to the top with a new time but still opens the earlier comment instead of the new one.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the updated notification links to the new comment that caused the update.
bugs.actual: The user read the first comment, pinned the notification, and the issue owner then posted a second comment. The pinned notification's time updated, but opening it scrolled to and highlighted the first comment, with the second comment below it.
reproSteps: As one user, create a public repository and an issue.
As a second user, subscribe to the issue without watching the repository.
As the owner, post a comment on the issue.
As the second user, open the notification to read the comment, then pin it from the Read tab.
As the owner, post a second comment.
As the second user, open the pinned notification from Notifications.
bugs.reason: Intended notification behavior. updateIssueNotification only moves a notification's target comment forward when the notification is Read; otherwise a new comment only updates its time and order, so the notification is never moved past comments the user may not have seen (models/activities/notification.go, go-gitea/gitea#8835). A pinned notification is never Read, so a new comment reorders it but keeps the comment it was pinned at. Opening it returns to that point in the conversation, with the newer comment directly below.

matchingGuidance.scope: Only reports that an updated pinned notification opens or highlights the earlier comment it was pinned at instead of the newest comment. Do not generalize to pinned notifications that disappear, become unreachable, change read state, or affect other notifications.
